plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and align with conservative limits.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
Focus on broad index and income for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential ~1.5%/month return. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure. Expect lower drawdowns but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Reduce all leveraged holdings (METU, SOXL, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to smaller allocations.
This lowers overall portfolio leverage and concentration.
Initiate a new position in NOW, a strong scanner setup, for growth and diversification.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name mandate.
Increase exposure to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to lean into growth.
Initiate a new, larger position in NOW, a top scanner setup, for aggressive growth.
This strategy uses leverage and concentration to target higher returns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4%/month. It significantly increases leverage and concentration in high-beta and leveraged ETFs. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown risk and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize monthly distributions and income.
Sell all leveraged and high-beta single names (METU, SOXL, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to near zero.
This shifts the portfolio towards a low-drawdown, income-generating structure.
Maintain a focus on steady distributions over growth.
income.read: This income plan aims to park cash for yield, targeting ~1%/month. It prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown by cutting leverage and high-beta names. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market downturns.
